title: Nifty slips below critical support level of 23,600 as market reacts to global economic uncertainties
summary: Indian equity indices experienced a decline on Monday, with the Nifty 50 falling below 23,800. Rising Brent crude oil prices and investor preference for smaller stocks impacted large-cap performance. The market also faces pressure from increased IPOs and fund-raising activities. US bond yields are nearing their 2023 highs, causing investor discomfort. Mid and small-cap segments show stronger activity while large caps lag.

title: Life insurers' new business premium up 33% in August
summary: Life insurers displayed impressive growth in new business premiums for August, with an overall year-on-year increase of thirty-three percent. This surge was predominantly driven by the single-premium and group business sectors, although retail-weighted premiums grew at a more moderate rate. Experts in the industry predict a return to more typical growth patterns in the following months.

title: Insurers seek greater flexibility in using equity derivatives for portfolio hedging
summary: Indian insurers are seeking greater flexibility in using equity derivatives, including allowing exposure to be aggregated across multiple funds rather than applying limits separately. The move could help insurers hedge broader equity portfolios, but adoption remains limited. Irdai allowed insurers to use equity derivatives solely for hedging existing equity exposures in February 2025.

title: Irdai fines ICICI Lombard Rs 1 crore for outsourcing, vendor management lapses
summary: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India has imposed a ₹1 crore penalty on ICICI Lombard General Insurance for lapses in outsourcing, vendor management and corporate governance. The regulator said the insurer failed to classify event management services involving agents of other insurers as outsourced activities or report related expenses.

title: Private banks’ profit margins recover as FCNR(B) inflows ease deposit funding pressure
summary: India’s private banks saw fresh lending spreads widen sharply in July as FCNR(B) inflows improved liquidity and reduced reliance on expensive wholesale funding. Fresh spreads rose 22 basis points to 3.13%, nearly double those at public sector banks. However, analysts cautioned that margin gains could prove gradual and difficult to sustain.

title: Fairfax plans IIFL Finance exit to fund IDBI Bank bid
summary: Fairfax Financial Holdings plans to exit IIFL Finance to fund its IDBI Bank acquisition.  The investor will use proceeds to part-fund the proposed takeover of the state-owned lender.  Fairfax intends to merge CSB Bank with IDBI Bank after completing the acquisition.  This move aims to simplify lending interests and avoid business overlaps.  The deal is expected to be completed shortly after procedural steps.

title: Indian firms line up $7.7 billion in ECB proposals in July
summary: Indian companies filed proposals worth $7.70 billion for external commercial borrowings in July. This represented a significant 27% growth over the previous month's figures. The Reserve Bank of India had eased its borrowing framework earlier in February. Air India and Interglobe Aviation together filed proposals worth $780 million. These companies sought special permissions from the central bank for their borrowings.

title: Gold loans, consumer durables drive NBFC credit growth to 14.9% in July
summary: Non-banking financial companies saw 14.9 percent credit expansion by July end. This growth accelerated from last year's 10.6 percent expansion. Gold loans surged 68.5 percent and consumer durable loans grew 51.5 percent. Retail loans within NBFCs increased 21.4 percent, showing strong performance. Housing and vehicle loans also recorded significant year-on-year growth.
